title: De Pijp (Oude and Nieuwe Pijp: 1870-1914 speculative rows)
evidence: scripts/block-face/types/de-pijp/*.json: ten measured Pijp house types (1875-1893), every one three axes of white T-windows on a 4.8-8 m front, a 4.1-4.7 m ground storey (shop or raised ground) under 2.7-3.3 m upper storeys, a white cornice and a slate roof behind it
pijp-1886-segmental-mansard (eaves 15.1 m), pijp-1889-five-storey-banded (15.2 m), pijp-1892-banded-keystone (14.0 m): four- and five-storey rows read 14-15.5 m to the cornice
Nicolaas Witsenkade and Den Texstraat types (witsen-1890-*, tex-188x-*): the slate attic behind the cornice rises at about 70 degrees with one dormer per front

wall.evidence: OKLab median of the 219 De Pijp rows measure-walls.ts read from panoramas (1059 pands; L 0.533, median C 0.017, 91 rows below C 0.012); the 113 unread rows take their street median or this pool, warmed like every brick wall (round 13)

ahnFrontForms.evidence: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat 157140 row (8 pands, 1875): 3DBAG lines 12.1 m where AHN4 reads the fronts at 13.6-14.0 m, each a gentle front (about 1 m per metre) with the steep rise behind it; the panorama shows four storeys and a cornice at about 14 m, not 12. De Pijp hides its pitched roofs behind a cornice, so the front height is the eaves

families.label: three-storey early Pijp row (eaves to about 12 m; pijp-1875-shop-dormer)
four-storey Pijp row (eaves 12-15.5 m): the district's main family (pijp-1882 to 1892 types)
five-storey Pijp row (eaves over 15.5 m; pijp-1889-five-storey-banded, Nieuwe Pijp)

pitched.evidence: the Pijp and Witsenkade types (witsen-1890-*, tex-1882-hood-bracket-mansard, pijp-1886-segmental-mansard): a slate attic behind the cornice at about 70 degrees, one dormer with a hoist beam per front; drawn where the series' 3DBAG rise is at least 2 m

notDrawn.what: the ground storey's shops are the retail look's (OSM shops); the row draws a residential ground storey
keystones, hoods and painted bands vary by builder within a street; unstated, the heads are plain (no dice)
